ENTRY.SYNOPSIS: Create a binned image of the empirical PSF matched up to be compatible with an image cut from a reference observed events file using the same spatial binning.

DESC.PARA: This script will create a binned FITS image of the empirical PSF compatible with an image binned from the input file.

SYNTAX.LINE: &upr; &cltool; infile=hrcf13182_repro_evt2.fits srcpos="22:08:40.7931 +45:44:32.691" outpsf=13182.psf outimg=13182.img samp=":300" binsize=0.2

&upr; &cltool; infile=hrcf18612_repro_evt2.fits srcpos="12:30:49.4181,+12:23:28.082" outpsf=empirical/18612-5.psf outimg=empirical/18612-5.img region="box(16655,16515,190,130)" binsize=0.25 bkgsubtract=no
&upr; &cltool; infile=hrcf18612_repro_evt2.fits srcpos="12:30:49.4181 +12:23:28.082" outpsf=empirical/18612-5.psf outimg=empirical/18612-5.img region="box.reg" binsize=0.25

&upr; &cltool; infile=hrcf18612_repro_evt2.fits srcpos="12:30:49.4181, +12:23:28.082" region="region(box.reg)" outpsf=empirical/18612-5.psf outimg=empirical/18612-5.img outdeconv=empirical/18612-5.deconv binsize=0.25 bkgsubtract=yes

&upr; &cltool; infile=hrcf18612_repro_evt2.fits srcpos="12:30:49.4181,+12:23:28.082" region="box.reg" outpsf=empirical/18612-5.psf outimg=empirical/18612-5.img outdeconv=empirical/18612-5.deconv binsize=0.25 verbose=1 clobber=yes mode=h bkgsubtract=no

PARAM.name: infile
PARAM.SYNOPSIS: The reference event file for which the empirical PSF will be tailored to, matching the detector orientation and the sky and WCS coordinate systems. Presently only HRC-I data is supported in this initial release.

DESC.PARA: This reference event file is typically the observed events file used with the 'format_empirical_psf' script to generate the unscaled background events file.

PARAM.name: srcpos
PARAM.SYNOPSIS: RA and DEC position of the source

DESC.PARA: This parameter defines the location of the source of interest that the PSF will be co-located in RA and Dec. The 'srcpos' should be within 0.5 arcmin of the detector aimpoint and within 0.02 mm of the best focus.

The 'srcpos' parameter is set as a space- or comma-separated value taken to be the Right Ascension and Declination to use (ICRS) in decimal degrees or colon-separated sexagesimal formats and must contain the "+" or "-" part of the declination. Examples include:
All positions must be in J2000.
The filtered, binned, and rotated empirical PSF image with its coordinates matching the input file and co-located on the 'srcpos' location.

PARAM.name: outimg
PARAM.SYNOPSIS: Output image file spatially binned — centered on the 'srcpos' location or if the 'region' parameter is set, the bounding box subtending the — and filtered based on the 'samp' range provided.

PARAM.name: outdeconv
PARAM.SYNOPSIS: Output deconvolved image file using the specified 'outpsf' and 'outimg' files with the number of iterations set by 'deconv_niter' utilizing the Lucy-Richardson algorithm.

PARAM.name: region
PARAM.SYNOPSIS: CIAO-formatted region expression or region file for the 'outimg' image file bounds. This should be in sky coordinates.

DESC.PARA: The binning factor has units of pixels, where the value need not be an integer for an events file, and may be be less than 1.

PARAM.name: samp
PARAM.SYNOPSIS: HRC event scaled summed amplifier tap signals (SAMP) range.

DESC.PARA: For HRC data, the scaled summed amplifier tap signal (SAMP) is an event attribute where high values greater than 300 are excluded in order to minimize the effect of the background.
This parameter is expressed as a range using DM filter syntax.

Events with low SAMP have larger uncertainties on the fine detector positions of events, and contribute to a small (<15%) inflation of the size of the PSF. However, due to the steady gain drop seen in the HRC, more events are now found with low values of SAMP, and this may have a proportionally larger effect on the observed size of point sources. In the event that higher sharpness is required, exclude SAMP values less than 16.

PARAM.name: bkgsubtract
PARAM.SYNOPSIS: Remove putative background events for the empirical PSF data set?

PARAM.name: random_seed
PARAM.SYNOPSIS: Random seed for randomization of background events to be removed if 'bkgsubtract=yes'.

PARAM.name: deconv_niter
PARAM.SYNOPSIS: Number of iterations using the Lucy-Richardson deconvolution algorithm via 'arestore'.

DESC.PARA: A few dozen to a hundred iterations should be used to avoid an overly grainy reconstruction with the Lucy-Richardson deconvolutuion algorithm.

There is no mathematically optimal number of iterations. Users should generally start with a generous number of iterations, 50 is a good starting point. Then increase the the number of iterations a few times in modest size increments, 10 is reasonable, to see how well the algorithm is converging. The increments can be increased or decreased based on scale of the total difference in the images.
Directory for storing temporary files that require further processing before becoming useful. If the directory does not exist then it will be created for use by the script, and then deleted.

PARAM.name: clobber
PARAM.SYNOPSIS: Specifies if an existing output file should be overwritten.

PARAM.name: verbose
PARAM.SYNOPSIS: Specifies the level of verbosity (0-5) in displaying diagnostic messages.

ADESC.title: Using the Empirical PSFs
ADESC.PARA: From the HRMA calibration group's "Chandra Empirical HRC PSF" page, the empirical PSFs are stacked from individual observations of a known point source where the roll has been corrected for and the x- and y-axes are aligned with the detector U and V coordinates.

Note that the process of generating the PSFs included identifying and filtering out tailgated events. This was done merely to use the best data from AR Lac, which flares frequently and often reaches high count rates (>5 ct/s) where tailgated photons become a significant fraction of the total. Most source brightnesses are well below this level and tailgating may be ignored. If there are any intervals with high count rates that occur due to flares or similar events, tailgated events can be excluded simply by excluding such intervals.
